rows: Cosmetic products made available in Great Britain must comply with applicable cosmetic-product rules.
A responsible person established in the UK is required.
A product safety assessment should be completed by a suitably qualified assessor.
A product information file should be maintained.
Products should be manufactured according to good manufacturing practice.
Specified labelling information must appear on the container or packaging.
Products should be notified to OPSS before being made available to consumers.
Serious undesirable effects and safety concerns require appropriate reporting and action.
An ingredient list or notification receipt does not prove that a cosmetic product is safe and compliant.
Conclusions require responsible person, assessment, file, manufacture, ingredients, label, notification and safety evidence.
Dangerous goods in passenger baggage can create a risk to flight safety.
Some articles are forbidden in both cabin and checked baggage.
Some articles are permitted only in cabin baggage or only under specified conditions.
Airline approval may be required for certain batteries, medical equipment or mobility aids.
Spare batteries and power banks require particular protection against short circuit.
Passengers should check current airline and CAA requirements before travel.
Damaged, defective or recalled batteries may be prohibited.
Operators and airports should provide clear dangerous-goods information to passengers.
An item being sold for travel or accepted on a previous flight does not prove it is permitted now.
Conclusions require item, energy or quantity, condition, packaging, baggage location, airline approval and current rules.
A 406 MHz beacon can alert search and rescue authorities through satellite systems.
EPIRBs are intended for vessels and may activate manually or automatically.
PLBs are personal devices that can be used in relevant environments.
UK-coded beacons should be registered with the UK Beacon Registry.
Registration information should be kept accurate and up to date.
Beacon identity should match the vessel or user records.
Beacons should be installed, tested and maintained according to applicable guidance.
Activation should be treated as a distress alert and false alerts should be reported promptly.
Possession or registration of a beacon does not prove that it is correctly installed and operational.
Conclusions require beacon type, coding, registration, battery, test, mounting, maintenance and vessel or user evidence.
Food information supplied on labels, notices or online must be accurate and not misleading.
Prepacked food generally requires a product name and ingredients list.
Specified allergens must be emphasised within the ingredients list where required.
Net quantity and date marking requirements apply to relevant foods.
Storage and use instructions should be provided when needed for safe use.
Business name and address information is generally required.
Origin information is required in specified circumstances.
Mandatory information should be legible and available before online purchase.
A professionally designed label or barcode does not prove compliance with food-information law.
Conclusions require product category, ingredients, allergens, quantity, date, storage, origin, business details and sales channel.
